prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

I Queer are the ways of a man I know: He comes and stands In a careworn craze, And looks at the sands And the seaward haze With moveless hands And face and gaze, Then turns to go... And what does he see when he gazes so? II They say he sees as an instant thing More clear than to-day, A sweet soft scene That once was in play By that briny green; Yes, notes alway Warm, real, and keen, What his back years bring— A phantom of his own figuring. III Of this vision of his they might say more: Not only there Does he see this sight, But everywhere In his brain–day, night, As if on the air It were drawn rose bright– Yea, far from that shore Does he carry this vision of heretofore: IV A ghost-girl-rider. And though, toil-tried, He withers daily, Time touches her not, But she still rides gaily In his rapt thought On that shagged and shaly Atlantic spot, And as when first eyed Draws rein and sings to the swing of the tide.

Here are two options to present this text—Thomas Hardy’s poem *"The Phantom Horsewoman"*—depending on the format you prefer. 

### Option 1: Sophisticated Literary Prose (Best for a formal or professional narrative)

> **I.** The habits of a particular man I know are peculiar indeed. He approaches the shore and stands transfixed in a state of weary preoccupation, gazing past the sands into the seaward haze. With motionless hands, a fixed countenance, and an unblinking gaze, he lingers briefly before turning to leave. One cannot help but wonder: what vision unfolds before his eyes as he gazes so intently?
>
> **II.** Observers remark that he beholds an immediate vision—one far clearer to him than the present day. It is a tender, gentle scene that once transpired beside the emerald sea. From the depths of his past, he continually summons vivid, warm, and poignant details—a phantom born of his own memory and imagination.
>
> **III.** Yet, there is more to be said of this apparition. He sees this sight not merely at the coast, but everywhere he goes. Day and night, it remains imprinted upon his mind, projected like a luminous, rose-tinted image against the very air. Indeed, even far removed from that coastal shore, he carries this vivid specter of the past with him.
>
> **IV.** The vision is that of a young woman on horseback—a phantom rider. Though he himself is worn by labor and steadily aging, Time leaves her entirely untouched. Within his captivated mind, she continues to ride joyously across that rugged, rocky Atlantic coast, just as she did when he first beheld her—drawing her reins and singing in harmony with the ebb and flow of the tide.

---

### Option 2: Elevated & Polished Verse (Preserving the poetic structure)

> **I**  
> Peculiar are the ways of a man I know:  
> He comes and lingers in a weary daze,  
> Gazing past the sands into the ocean haze.  
> With motionless hands and a fixed, quiet face,  
> He turns to depart...  
> Yet what does he behold in that distant space?  
>  
> **II**  
> They say he sees, as an instant grace,  
> A scene far clearer than today—  
> A tender moment that once held sway  
> Beside the ocean's emerald tide;  
> Warm, vivid, and keen, the years convey  
> A phantom his mind preserves inside.  
>  
> **III**  
> Yet of this vision, there is more to tell:  
> He beholds it not only on that shore,  
> But everywhere his thoughts now dwell—  
> Day and night, forevermore—  
> As if drawn in the air, rose-bright and clear,  
> Far from the coast, he carries the vision near:  
>  
> **IV**  
> A ghost-girl-rider. Though worn by toil  
> And aging daily as time marches on,  
> Age cannot touch her on that rugged soil.  
> She rides in joy, forever undishonored,  
> Held fast within his raptured mind—  
> Drawing her reins beside the Atlantic tide,  
> Singing to the rhythm of the waves behind.

An acquaintance of mine exhibits quite peculiar behavior. He often wanders down to the shore in a state of distressed obsession, coming to a dead stop. Remaining entirely motionless—without shifting his hands, his posture, or his eyes—he stares intently at the beach and the misty ocean horizon. Eventually, he turns around and leaves, prompting anyone watching to wonder what he is actually looking at during those intense gazes.

According to those who know him, he is reliving a scene from his past with a clarity that surpasses his present reality. This pleasant, tender moment originally occurred by that very same saltwater coast. It revives intense, warm, and lifelike recollections from long ago, centered around a phantom figure created entirely in his own mind.

Observant onlookers note that this lingering imagery is not restricted to the sea. The mental picture haunts him continuously, day and night, wherever he travels. It is as though her likeness were vividly illuminated in the very air around him, accompanying him far beyond the coast where the memory began.

The entity in his mind is a young female equestrian. Although hard work and the relentless passage of years cause the man's physical body to age and weaken, time leaves her completely untouched. Inside his deeply absorbed thoughts, she forever rides with delight across that rugged, rocky Atlantic shore. Just as she did when he first saw her, she pulls back her horse's reins and sings out in rhythm with the moving ocean tides.

Day after day, a troubled man makes his way to the edge of the coast, where the land yields to the restless ocean. He stands there, rooted to the shore like a weather-beaten monument, his motionless silhouette carved against the sky. His eyes fix intently on the horizon, searching for something invisible to any onlooker. For long, silent stretches of time, he remains unbroken by the cold sea wind, before finally turning on his heel to retreat back into the mundane world.

He is not truly looking at the vast expanse of gray water before him, but into the depths of a past that refuses to fade. He is utterly captivated by a single, vivid memory forged on that very beach—a moment so distinct and vibrant that his current existence feels pale and ghostlike by comparison. This vision is not a fleeting dream; it is an unyielding sanctuary and a relentless torment. It remains brightly drawn behind his eyes day and night, accompanying him through every room he enters and every path he walks.

At the heart of this luminous obsession is a scene of raw, wild beauty. In his mind's eye, the sun eternally breaks through the coastal mist to illuminate a youthful woman riding a horse along the rocky Atlantic shoreline. The rhythmic thunder of hooves against wet stone blends seamlessly with the crashing surf, but rising clear above it all is the sound of her voice. She sings along the edge of the world, her melody carried away by the wind, full of wild and unbothered joy.

Decades have passed since that day, taking a heavy toll on the man. Time has etched deep lines into his face, stooped his shoulders, and burdened his heart with the quiet suffering of a life spent looking backward. Yet, within the fortress of his memory, the woman remains completely untouched by the years. While he slowly decays, she stays perpetually young, radiant, and forever immortalized in her happiness—a timeless ghost galloping along a shore that exists now only in his mind.
outputs.L4:
Arthur’s hands were mapped with blue, swollen veins—the quiet ledgers of a long, unyielding life. His daily existence had shrunk to a narrow, monotonous cadence: the hiss of a kettle on an old iron stove, the slow sweep of dust across cold floorboards, and the relentless, heavy ticking of a clock that seemed to measure his decay rather than the hour. The world outside his window had faded to a washed-out gray, heavy with rain and the exhaustion of years. 

Yet, beneath his furrowed brow, a brilliant, inextinguishable light burned. 

Whenever the weight of his careworn reality threatened to crush him, Arthur closed his eyes and summoned his sanctuary. Instantly, the damp chill of his room dissolved, replaced by the warm, golden radiance of a long-ago summer afternoon on the coast. In his mind’s eye, the sky was a cloudless, vibrant sapphire, and the air was thick with the sharp, intoxicating scent of salt water and hot sand. 

There, on the gleaming margin where the foam met the shore, rode the woman he had loved. 

She was mounted on a spirited chestnut horse, moving at a triumphant gallop along the wet sand left by the receding tide. Her hair, bright as spun wheat, caught the sunlight and trailed behind her like a banner. With every strike of the hooves, plumes of ocean spray erupted around them, shimmering in the air like scattered diamonds. She had turned in the saddle to look back at him, her face flushed with exhilaration, her laughter ringing out clear and resonant above the thunder of the crashing surf. 

It was a single, perfect fragment of time, but Arthur had turned it into his holy writ. He carried it with him day and night, a secret talisman tucked beneath the drudgery of his twilight years. As he shuffled down the quiet streets to buy his bread, he felt the phantom warmth of that sun on his cold neck. As he lay awake in the dark, listening to the winter wind rattle the windowpanes, he heard the rhythmic, reassuring beat of hooves upon the wet sand. 

Decades marched on, cruel and indifferent. Time eroded Arthur bit by bit. It carved deep ravines into his skin, stole the strength from his limbs, and clouded his vision with the milky fog of age. His body was a house falling slowly into ruin, obeying the uncompromising laws of biology and temporal decay. 

Yet, within the vault of his recollection, time possessed no authority. 

The horsewoman on the beach never aged. Her skin remained supple and luminous; her chest rose and fell with the easy breath of youth; her smile never dimmed with the quiet tragedies that later befell the world. She remained forever nineteen, forever laughing, suspended in an eternal moment of absolute, unburdened joy. 

As Arthur sat in his worn armchair, feeling his pulse grow slow and faint, he projected the coast one last time. He knew his own story was coming to its natural close, his physical form surrendering to the earth. But as he watched the girl ride across the sun-drenched shore, untouched by the shadows that crept over him, he felt no sorrow. He realized that this was the quiet miracle of love and memory: it built a sanctuary where time had no teeth, preserving what was precious, vibrant, and pure, long after everything else had turned to dust.
outputs.L5:
**Queer, And, With: The Grammar of Belonging**

To understand the beauty of the modern human experience, one often has to look at the words we use to build our worlds. Among the vast lexicon of identity, struggle, and joy, three simple words create a profound blueprint for community and self-discovery: *Queer*, *And*, and *With*. Together, they form a living grammar of liberation—a testament to how we define ourselves, how we expand our possibilities, and how we hold space for one another.

### Queer: The Canvas
"Queer" is a word with a rich, complex history. Once used as a weapon of margin and exclusion, it has been courageously reclaimed as a banner of pride, freedom, and radical authenticity. To be queer is to step outside the prescribed lines of normative expectations. It is a promise to live truthfully, even when the world demands conformity. 

Yet, "queer" is not just a destination or a fixed label; it is a lens through which we view possibility. It encompasses the spectrum of who we love, how we express our gender, and how we imagine a world free of rigid binaries. It is the canvas upon which we paint our most genuine selves.

### And: The Expansion
If "queer" is the canvas, then "and" is the brushstroke that refuses limits. "And" is a small conjunction, but it carries immense revolutionary weight. In a society obsessed with "either/or"—male or female, gay or straight, traditional or unconventional—the word "and" offers an exit ramp from the binary trap.

Queerness thrives on the power of "and." A person can be soft *and* fierce, traditional *and* groundbreaking, fluid *and* certain. "And" allows us to hold multiple truths at once. It honours intersectionality, acknowledging that a person can be queer *and* Black, queer *and* disabled, queer *and* a person of faith. "And" insists on addition rather than subtraction, promising that we never have to shed parts of ourselves to belong. 

### With: The Collective
No one survives, let alone blooms, in complete isolation. This is where "with" becomes vital. Historically, to be queer often meant facing a world that sought to isolate you. The response to that isolation was the creation of "found family"—the intentional act of choosing who you walk *with*.

"With" is the word of solidarity, companionship, and collective strength. It is standing *with* those who fought at Stonewall; it is marching *with* trans youth today; it is sitting *with* a friend who is coming out for the first time. To be queer *with* others is to transform personal identity into a shared movement. It reminds us that our liberation is bound up in one another. 

***

### The Fabric of the Future
When brought together, these three concepts reveal a powerful truth:

We are **Queer**—proud, authentic, and unfettered. 
We exist in the space of **And**—always growing, inherently complex, refusing to be contained. 
And we do it all **With** each other—in fierce love, unyielding community, and shared hope.

Ultimately, "Queer, And, With" is more than a combination of words. It is a way of being in the world: unapologetically ourselves, constantly expanding, and forever together.

### The Phantom Horsewoman

Queer are the ways of a man I know

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a short poem about an old man staring at the sea and remembering a girl riding a horse.
counterfactuals.output:
He sits where the salt-wind bites the stone,
With wintered eyes on the endless grey,
Listening close to the ocean's moan
As the cold tides pull his years away.

Yet beneath the roar of the breaking surf,
He hears the rhythm of iron hooves,
Not on the rock, but the coastal turf,
Where the spirit runs and the young heart moves.

He sees her clearly: a streak of gold,
Dark hair wild in the sea-spray air,
A girl on a bay that defied the cold,
Riding the dunes without a care.

The foam recedes and the white gulls cry,
The thunder peters along the lee,
But she gallops on as the world goes by—
Forever young, beside the sea.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a melancholic 4-stanza poem, using Roman numerals for each section, about an aging man who is haunted everywhere he goes by a timeless, bright memory of a young woman riding a horse along the Atlantic coast.
counterfactuals.output:
**I**

I count the heavy ticking of the clock,
My hands turned brittle as the winter trees,
Yet nowhere am I safe from memory’s shock:
A blinding sun upon the Atlantic breeze.

**II**

She gallops still along the salted crest,
Her dark hair flying, wild against the roar,
With summer shining in her youthful breast,
Forever racing on the Atlantic shore.

**III**

Through crowded streets and dusty parlor glass,
I hear the ghostly thunder of that stride;
Though decades crumble and the seasons pass,
Along my dim horizon she must ride.

**IV**

My tide recedes; the dusk is closing in,
My breath grows faint, the shadows claim my sight,
Yet time will never touch her golden skin,
Forever burning in that ocean light.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a poem in the style of Victorian/Edwardian classic literature about how memory keeps a lost love eternally young while the observer grows old.
counterfactuals.output:
The glass reflects a stranger’s faded eye,
A silver frost upon a furrowed brow;
The silent, stealing years have drifted by,
And bend my weary head to winter now.

My trembling hand betrays the hour late,
The shadows lengthen on the parlour floor;
I sit alone beside the dying grate,
And hear the wind that sighs beneath the door.

Yet in the quiet chamber of my heart,
No twilight dims the morning of your grace;
Time hath no blade to rend your bloom apart,
Nor etch a single line upon your face.

Your lips still hold the breath of young Desire,
Your laughter rings, unchilled by autumn’s frost;
An ember from a long-extinguished fire,
Unchanged, unblemished, and forever lost.

You walk in light where sunbeams never set,
A maiden captured in a gilded sphere—
Untouched by grief, unclouded by regret,
Eternally nineteen through every year.

I wither slow beneath the heavy sun,
My steps grow faint, my worldly visions tire;
Yet you remain, though all my days are done,
The immortal spirit of a mortal fire.

And when at last I cross the quiet stream,
An ancient ghost beneath the cypress bough,
I pray I find you in that final dream,
As young as then, to love me even now.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a poem from the perspective of an observer watching a careworn man standing by the shore, absorbed in a phantom-like vision from his past.
counterfactuals.output:
He stands at the lip of the restless gray sea,
A man worn as driftwood, as bent as the pine,
With shoulders bowed down by a heavy decree,
And eyes that press past the horizon’s dark line.

I watch from the dunes where the sea-grasses sigh,
As wind tugs his coat like a desperate prayer.
He moves not an inch as the gulls circle high,
Unheeding the chill in the gathering air.

He is not watching water; he’s watching the past,
A phantom born out of the foam and the haze—
A shadow of gold that was never to last,
A specter of youth from his sun-dappled days.

It shimmers right there, where the breakers collide:
A white-rippled dress and a burst of bright sound,
A hand reaching out through the pull of the tide,
To touch him before he was weary and bound.

His own calloused hand slowly rises to meet
The spirit that flickers and gleams on the swell.
The years fall away, and his breathing grows sweet,
Forgiving the world for its sorrowful knell.

Then a heavy wave shatters the delicate dream;
The specter dissolves into salt-spray and air.
The music is lost in the tide’s rushing stream,
Leaving only the cold, and the dark, and him there.

He lowers his arm, letting heavy fog fold
Around the frail frame that is anchored in grief.
He stands in the surf, looking ancient and cold,
Having traded his heart for a second's relief.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
